title: scale-up gate: refuse the Kafka controller-leader (--force-primary override)
description: The cluster-safety gate of scale-up (GAP #4, batch 3) shown on Kafka. scale-up resolves a broker VM to its per-region adapter (kafka-east-1 -> the `kafka-east` KafkaClusterAdapter; the meta `kafka` adapter delegates CanResizeVm to the region owning the VM) and gates on the KRaft controller-leader: KafkaClusterAdapter.CanResizeVm returns false when the target's live role is `controller-leader`, so a resize of the leader is refused (it would power-cycle the controller / write window). A follower/non-leader broker passes the gate; --force-primary is the explicit override. This demo only exercises the NON-destructive refusal path (a real follower resize would cold-restart a live broker -- see the handbook playbook for the follower + override commands). Live-verified 2026-07-06 on kafka-east: scale-up of the controller-leader (kafka-east-1) was refused ('... pass --force-primary'); a follower (kafka-east-2) passed the gate.

prerequisites.smokeGate: nexus-infra-kafka smoke-0.H.2 ALL GREEN; kafka-east-1 is the CURRENT controller-leader (KRaft leadership drifts -- if not, target the leader shown in step 1)

observe.what: exactly one member has role=controller-leader (the KRaft quorum leader); the other controllers are controller-follower. This is the role the gate reads via CanResizeVm. A follower here is eligible for a no-force resize.

REFUSED: "'kafka-east-1' is the current primary/leader of cluster 'kafka-east'; resizing it now would disrupt the write window. Fail over first, or pass --force-primary to override." Exit code 2 -- the VM is NOT powered off. The meta adapter routed the gate to kafka-east via the vm-name region match; the resolution is locked by a unit test.

whatProves: scale-up's cluster-safety gate is Kafka-aware: it resolves a broker to its region adapter and refuses to power-cycle the KRaft controller-leader (protecting the write window), returning exit 2 without touching the VM. A controller-follower passes the gate (a no-force resize proceeds); --force-primary overrides the refusal on the leader -- both shown in the handbook playbook.
